title: About What You Would Expect From Sawdust and Glue
text:
About What You Would Expect From Sawdust and Glue. Where oh where to begin. I needed a functional piece of furniture for my artist studio. Someplace for a printer and a cutting machine etc. When I had the chance to get this from the Vine I went for it.

Pros:
Attractive from a distance.

Cons:

**Not at all white. The color is what I would call antique white. Matches well in my room.

**Poorly packaged. When UPS delivered it, there was packaging hanging out all over the torn up box. Fortunately it wasn't damaged.

**Assembly was interesting to say the least.

You definitely need 2 people and a power drill to put this together. The instructions are pictorial and assume a great amount of knowledge that the average person probably doesn't have. Like putting glue on the dowels before you insert them. No where does it tell you that. This took about 4 hours from start to finish. Be sure you assemble this very close to where you want it to land because it is the finest 130 pounds of sawdust and glue you will ever move.

**Has weight restrictions. In the instructions there are pretty clear weight limits for every part of this piece. Nothing should be set on top of it. No books. Nothing very heavy. About what you expect for something that is doweled, glued and screwed through poor quality particle board.

**Poor quality for the money. There are various qualities of particle board, some are quite sturdy. This is low end at best. I do not expect this to have a really long lifespan. Should probably not be moved around much as this will surely cause it to fall apart.
